Commentary.Commentary: The Kiwis continue their Asian adventure as after their tour of Bangladesh for just a 5-game T20I series, their ship has docked at the shores of Pakistan for a 3-game ODI series, following which, there will be a 5-game T20I series. The 50-over series will be kickstarting this tour and both teams will be looking to gain some momentum starting this tour by winning this series. First things first, this series will NOT BE A PART of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup Super League, due to the unavailability of the Decision Review System (DRS) and hence, it will only be a bilateral series. Safe to say, that this series does not hold too much of an impact in a larger sense, but both teams will still want to give it their all. Pakistan have named a strong squad for this series and will have the likes of Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan, Fakhar Zaman, Shaheen Afridi, Hasan Ali in their ranks, and on paper at least, they look like the stronger side. They have also included 4 uncapped players with the likes of batsman Mohammad Haris, pacers Mohammad Wasim and Shahnawaz Dhani, and also spinner Zahid Mahmood, and Pakistan will be hoping to hand all of them a chance in this series. The Black Caps' squad looks slightly thin due to the non-availability of their star players but they still have enough firepower to cause an upset. With no Kane Williamson in their ranks, they will be under the leadership of Tom Latham. They are stacked with allrounders for this ODI series and we should be seeing quite a few of them take part. Unfortunately, they will be without the services of Tom Blundell for this ODI series, due to a left quad strain and he will be replaced by Daryl Mitchell, who will be available only after the second ODI, after completing the mandatory isolation. Pakistan are favourites heading into this series but do not be surprised if the Kiwis punch above their weight.
